blocking.title: Verify the CSP and ACL on a real Mac after #153 (PR #158)
blocking.detail: The webview now runs under a Content-Security-Policy and every app command is gated per window, neither of which can be exercised headless — and neither is exercised by `pnpm dev` either: Tauri only injects the CSP into assets it serves itself, and in dev the page comes straight from Vite, so a green dev run proves nothing. Test a bundled build: `pnpm tauri build --debug` is the fast path (the release bundle works too). In it: project logos render (they are `data:` URIs), the Analytics charts render (Recharts inline styles), Settings -> App -> Check for updates reaches GitHub, and Settings -> App -> Reset / Uninstall raise a native warning sheet attached to the main window whose Cancel reports "Cancelled. Nothing was changed." inline. Then the tray panel: it opens, resizes to its card, Esc hides it, Scan now / Open app / Quit work — it had no capability at all before this PR, so this is the first time its window calls are actually allowed. A CSP violation shows in the webview console (right-click -> Inspect in a debug bundle) as "Refused to …".

blocking.title: Confirm the window drags and the layouts hold on a real Mac (#165)
blocking.detail: The three fixes for the owner's v0.1.1 report are verified by browser measurement and by tests over the capability files, but none of them can be exercised headless. In a bundled build (`pnpm tauri build --debug`): drag the window by the empty part of any screen's toolbar and by the strip above the sidebar's logo — that was permission-denied before, so it is the one thing that either works or does not. Then resize down to the 720x480 minimum: the sidebar's recents list should scroll with its footer still pinned and visible, the Detail screen should stack its scorecard under the source instead of squeezing the code to a 61px column, and no screen should scroll sideways. Check a project with a long name — the toolbar's buttons should keep their shape and the name should ellipsize.

blocking.title: Set POLAR_PRO_PRODUCT_ID before deploying the fulfillment worker
blocking.detail: After #154 the worker refuses to mint unless wrangler.toml's [vars] POLAR_PRO_PRODUCT_ID equals the Pro product's id from the Polar dashboard (the value must live in the file — `wrangler deploy` overwrites dashboard vars — and sandbox and production orgs have different ids). Create the Pro product, paste its id, then `pnpm deploy` from fulfillment/. Verify in sandbox: an order for Pro mints and emails; an order for any other product produces a 202 and a 'not for the licensed product' log line; an empty value answers 500 and mints nothing.

blocking.title: Lock the GitHub account and repo around the flip to public (audit I-4, M-4)
blocking.detail: Settings only, no code — but the order matters because branch/tag rules and environment reviewers are Pro-plan features while a repo is private and free once it is public. Now, while private: (1) two-factor auth on the account; (2) Actions → General: 'Require approval for all outside collaborators' and default workflow permissions 'Read repository contents'; (3) Settings → Environments → create `release` so the next tag push does not create it implicitly. Then flip public. Immediately after: (4) `release` environment → add yourself as required reviewer — until this is done `environment: release` in release.yml is a no-op and a tag push still builds and signs unattended, exactly as before; (5) Rules → tag ruleset for `v*` so only you can create release tags; (6) branch protection on `main` (require PR + green CI). The next `v*` tag is the first live run of the pinned tauri-action and the environment gate.

blocking.title: Re-verify the menu-bar panel on a real Mac after the #145 fixes
blocking.detail: The first on-device pass found four visual defects (#145), all fixed: the tray icon is now a black-and-alpha template image, the score ring's type scales with its diameter, the popover window resizes to the height of its card, and the fix rows carry one grade badge instead of a glyph-plus-chip pair. Re-check on-device: the menu-bar icon is a legible glyph that tints for the light and dark bar and inverts when clicked; the panel window hugs its content with no dead gap in any state (no-scan, nothing-to-fix, three fixes, scanning, failure) and scrolls rather than overflowing when tall; the 56 px ring's letter sits inside its stroke and the score reads on the header's meta line. Then the original checklist: left-click opens under the icon, second click closes, outside click closes, far-left/right clamps inside the screen, multi-monitor with mixed scale factors opens on the right display, transparent corners, Esc hides, reopening refetches, a fix row / chip / Open app raises the main window, Scan now shows the bar and refreshes at the end, Quit exits. Checklist: .superpowers/sdd/2026-08-23-menu-bar-panel/task-2-report.md

blocking.title: Mint the production license keypair
blocking.detail: After merging PR #69: cd src-tauri && cargo run --bin license-tool -- keygen. Store the private key in your password manager, paste the printed PUBKEY array into src-tauri/src/license.rs, commit. The current embedded key's private seed was discarded after minting your own dev pro key, so no customer keys can be minted today — and re-keygening invalidates that dev key (mint yourself a fresh one). Only you should ever hold this key.

marketing.title: Apple Developer Program — signing & notarization
marketing.detail: Without it the DMG triggers Gatekeeper warnings (right-click → Open still works; acceptable for early adopters, fatal for broad marketing). Enroll ($99/yr), create a Developer ID Application cert, then add repo secrets: APPLE_CERTIFICATE, APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD, APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY, APPLE_ID, APPLE_PASSWORD, APPLE_TEAM_ID. The release workflow picks them up automatically — no code change needed.

decisions.title: Store the AI API key in the macOS keychain instead of the settings table
decisions.detail: The provider API key is written to the `settings` table in plaintext today, so anyone with read access to the app's SQLite file has it. Moving it to the macOS keychain (Tauri's keyring plugin or the Security framework) is the fix; decide whether it blocks the first release or lands right after.

decisions.title: Decide phase 2 scope: evidence-backed findings + diff apply
decisions.detail: With usage evidence now landing, decide whether phase 2 should turn it into evidence-backed findings (e.g. 'unused skill', 'MCP server never called') and/or let fixes be diff-applied directly from the Setup screen.

decisions.title: Version number for launch
decisions.detail: Ship as v0.1.0 (honest early-access) or v1.0.0 (marketing-friendly)? The bump script handles either.

decisions.title: Auto-update: in v1 or after?
decisions.detail: Tauri's updater needs its own signing keypair and an update manifest endpoint. Recommendation: ship v1 without it, add in v1.1 — early users will re-download.

decisions.title: Windows / Linux support
decisions.detail: Everything is Tauri so it's mostly build-matrix work, but tray/notification/QA effort is real. Post-v1 unless the market pulls for it.
